scope: Eliminate repeated filesystem target resolution during eligible exact workspace alias setup while preserving fallback, name-dependent public-table behavior, reloads and finite retention; local macOS arm64.
changes: Memoize normalized target paths by the complete ordered replacement list, only when the existing ordering/uniqueness/nonempty-table invariant permits direct exact alias resolution.
Borrow cache keys from the config; admit owned target values and known records before retention. Charge lookup hashing on every hit/miss and retain package-membership and alias-string admissions.
Keep the cache within one setup call, preserve general first-match lookup for caller-created tables, and keep prior published mappings on quota failure.

Feature-gated Hotpath measurement of uncached alias target resolution verifies 16 lookups for 512 aliases/16 lists and 64 lookups for 4096 aliases/64 lists. No public signature, field, dependency or check command changes.

cases: Repeated and reversed ordered replacements, first-existing fallback, deepest package membership, outside targets and new fallback files between setup calls.
Two exact aliases sharing replacement lists still resolve to different members through an earlier wildcard in an ineligible public table.
64 distinct generated targets exhaust a 4096-byte payload quota with sticky failure and preserve the previous map; a subsequent healthy setup completes.

"""Run sequential normal-binary comparisons after checks and builds have exited."""
from pathlib import Path
import os
import subprocess
import sys

area=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
assert 'HOTPATH_OUTPUT_PATH' not in os.environ
for workload in ['fan-in','call-heavy','monorepo','directory-index']:
    command=[sys.executable,'-B','scripts/benchmark.py','--binary',str(area/'after-jscycles'),'--baseline',str(area/'before-jscycles'),'--workload',workload,'--files','10000','--samples','21','--output',str(area/f'{workload}-comparison.json')]
    if workload=='monorepo': command += ['--packages','64','--aliases','4096']
    print('Running',command,flush=True)
    subprocess.run(command,check=True,timeout=180)

"""Retain checked profiles and verify distinct-target lookup cardinality."""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

area=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
out=area/'hotpath';out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
for workload in ['fan-in','call-heavy','monorepo','directory-index']:
    for suffix in ['', '-benchmark']:
        source=Path('target/tooling/hotpath')/f'{workload}{suffix}.json'
        json.loads(source.read_text());shutil.copy2(source,out/source.name)
path=out/'monorepo-large.json'
path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
command=[sys.executable,'-B','scripts/benchmark.py','--workload','monorepo','--files','10000','--packages','64','--aliases','4096','--samples','3','--output',str(out/'monorepo-large-benchmark.json')]
subprocess.run(command,env=dict(os.environ,HOTPATH_OUTPUT_PATH=str(path)),check=True,timeout=180)
for workload,expected in [('monorepo',16),('monorepo-large',64)]:
    profile=json.loads((out/f'{workload}.json').read_text())
    rows=profile['functions_timing']['data']
    row=next(row for row in rows if row['name'].endswith('resolve_alias_target_uncached'))
    assert row['calls']==expected,(workload,row)
    print(workload,expected,'uncached ordered target lists',flush=True)
shutil.copy2('target/release/jscycles',area/'profile-jscycles')

performance.method: 21 alternating samples plus one warm-up per saved normal binary on each same corpus. Checks, builds and mutation/Miri jobs complete before timing. JSON outputs agree byte for byte. Instrumented profiling follows timing in a separate build; restore the normal release binary afterward.
performance.limits: Warm synthetic local measurements; no customer latency budget, cold-cache, cross-platform, statistical significance, madge comparison or universal speedup claim. Previous per-alias call frequency is inferred from the old loop; new distinct-target call counts are observed in Hotpath.

unchanged.note: Manifests, locks, check commands, public doctest and parser/FFI code are unchanged. Miri retains its pure-code selection; new filesystem regressions are native. Previous sanitizer campaigns retain their original input scopes.

limitations: Local evidence does not execute hosted release targets, Windows-only paths or Linux-only filesystem cases.
No full Rust-OE certification, remote-input isolation, live reload, commit, push or publication.
